findings.issue: This is a known load-sensitive row with no owner and no disposition. Each awaitClosed is a fixed 10 s wall-clock wait. The w20-redeliver seat saw it fail once in a whole-package run under co-load (44.9 s test, about 9 s alone) and routed it to 'whoever owns delivery_ack_groupcommit_test.go'. Nobody took it. It runs in the pre-freeze `internal` step (-p 2, co-load) and in release-check's shared pass (default -p, about 22). A red there refuses the freeze or stops release-check at its first FAIL.
findings.evidence: w20-redeliver/report.md Open issues: 'TestDeliveryJournal_AckCheckRunsAfterEvaluationAndImmediatelyBeforeAppend failed once in a whole-package run under co-load. Its awaitClosed fixed 10 s bound (ingestACKWait) fired after a 44.9 s test ... passed 10/10 in isolation.' Needs owner: 'Route the load-sensitive ...'. No later commit touches the file (`git log d20309c0..2bf29705 -- internal/daemon/delivery_ack_groupcommit_test.go` is empty). No ledger mention.
findings.fix: Remove the wall-clock verdict. Wait on the gate and seal channels the row already controls, with no timeout, and leave hang detection to go test -timeout. Or record a ledger ruling that classifies a red from this row in the night. Pin it with -count=20 under QOMPACK_UNDER_COLOAD at -p 4.

findings.issue: A carried wall-clock dependency has no owner (w19c rehydrate open issue). The ObservePrompt seam runs on a goroutine, and dispatchOp waits at most 250 ms from the request's TS before returning Empty. The test asserts `calls == 1` immediately after dispatchOp returns, and the test is t.Parallel. If the seam goroutine is not scheduled within 250 ms (race lanes, release-check -p 22), calls is 0 and the row fails.
findings.evidence: handlers.go: `budget := d.promptReplyBudget(ts)`, then a `select { case r := <-ch: ... case <-wait.Done(): ... }` that returns hookio.Empty() without waiting for the seam. daemon_test.go:1650-1652 asserts `require.Equal(t, 1, calls, ...)`. w19-rehydrate/report-19c.md Open issues: 'Carried: ... depends on the wall clock ... It needs an injected clock or a seam-completion channel'.
findings.fix: Have the test seam close a channel and wait on it (or use require.Eventually) before asserting calls==1. That keeps the passive-reply assertion and removes the 250 ms dependency.

findings.location: internal/daemon/drain.go:727 (durableEnd(..., unchanged && memo.synced)) and drain.go:1300-1301 (durableEnd returns synced=false for a WAL segment the ingest holds)
findings.issue: The new sync-skip has one durability precondition, and no row pins it: the memo may skip the sync only when this drainer's own sync covered the file (memo.synced). Consider a WAL segment a full Drain read while the ingest held it. That pass read only up to the ingest's synced size and wrote its memo with synced=false. If the ingest then releases the segment with no further write, for example closing it after a failed Sync, the next pass must sync the segment before it reads the unsynced tail. Two mutants break that rule and every row stays green: dropping the `&& memo.synced` conjunct, and returning synced=true for a held segment. Under either one, the drain leases the bytes in that tail with no sync at all. That is the orphan-lease hole durableEnd exists to close. The product code is correct today; nothing in the tests protects it.

findings.issue: The round-2 fix, where readTo stops at the first line a pass read and left under no lease, is pinned only for a left line behind a waiting head, so always at an offset above 0. The most natural position is the file's first line: for example, a one-line client spool whose lease lookup hits a rotating or briefly unowned journal (leaseHeld then returns an error). Nothing pins that case. Mutating `>= 0` to `> 0` leaves every row green. Under that mutant, the silent drop the round-2 review found comes back: the next pass consumes the line in order as unadmitted, below readTo, with no drain_unadmitted count and no LOUD line. The product code is correct today.

findings.issue: pendingBlobOf replaced readBlob as the way a consumed line that is not published (absorbed, retired or denied) names its cleanup intent. It is meant to repeat readBlob's pre-read checks. Only its safeBlobName check is pinned (R3, the nosafe mutant). The no-Event, regular-file and size checks can each be removed, or all three together, and every row stays green. If they regressed, a denied or absorbed line naming a directory, a symlink or a wrong-size file called blob-*.bin would record an intent that readBlob would never have produced. cleanupAcknowledged would then os.Remove that entry. A non-empty directory would fail removeBlob on every pass, and with it cleanupAcknowledged, so every pass would return an error.
findings.evidence:
- Memo rows: 'mb_noregular SURVIVED | ok 200.999s', 'msz_nosize SURVIVED | ok 126.767s', 'mev_noevent SURVIVED | ok 110.278s'.
- Combined mutant mbs_all ('req.Event == nil' dropped, and the whole Lstat condition reduced to 'err != nil || fi == nil') against the broad drain set: 'mbs_all SURVIVED | ok 192.891s'.
- Code: removeBlob (blob.go:118-133) returns 'blob cleanup unavailable' for any os.Remove error other than not-exist. cleanupAcknowledged then joins that error into the pass's result.

findings.issue: This wave-20 row adds 37-50 s of Windows wall time to every internal/daemon run (about 7% of the package), but it only judges operation counts. Almost all of that time goes to the fixture's first pass, which makes 600 durable publications. The proof does not need 600 of them. It runs on every hosted daemon job (test x3 OS, stubskips, cover, release-dry-run, nightly race), and under -race it will cost several times more.
findings.evidence: `go test -p 1 -count=1 -json -run '^(<52 tests added since 738d67c7>)$' ./internal/daemon` reports this row at 49.52 s. The next slowest new row takes 2.49 s, and all 52 new rows together take 74.4 s. An overlay probe (C:/Users/Quant/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/qompack-audit2/regress/probe/zz_audit_probe_test.go, the same body with phase timers) gave: setup daemon 74 ms, fixture 192 ms, first pass 34.36 s (journal=5107 admitted=1501), second pass 2.32 s (journal=2107 admitted=301), PASS 37.47 s. Every assertion is a count bound (journalQueriesPerLine*(1+waiting+consumed), admitted[other]==0, syncs==0) and none is a time.
findings.fix: Shrink the fixture to waiting=30, consumed=60 (or 50/100). Each bound is linear in those constants, and the c7 failure shape (consumed lines re-admitted and re-journalled, plus an L x D re-attempt) still fails by orders of magnitude at that size. Alternatively, keep 300/600 behind testing.Short() off in the timing lane. Do not lose the first-pass journal bound.

nits.location: internal/daemon/drain.go:1447 (rememberFile carry: `if start >= readPos && len(lines) < orderingProcessedCap`)
nits.issue: The spoolMemo doc says a memo holds at most orderingProcessedCap lines per file. The only thing that keeps that true across an early-stopped pass is the cap in the carry-forward loop, and no row pins it. Without the cap, a pass that stops early carries every earlier line at or past readPos on top of the up to 4096 it consumed. Repeated stops then let one file's memo grow past the cap.

nits.issue:
Several new branches survive mutation and are not recorded as deliberate defence. Commit 3f705053 did record three others: the end-of-file guard, memoOf's shrink check and the unlisted-memo deletion.

nits.location: docs/architecture.md:191-193 and internal/daemon/drain.go:86-88 (withPassBudget doc: 'the pass reads each file's unconsumed lines once more, at its start')
nits.issue: Both texts say a pass reads the spool for blob references once, at its start, while an intent waits. That is exact only for a pass that moves no front. After every file whose front moved, drain.go:1259-1263 runs cleanupAcknowledged again, and pendingBlobReferences re-reads every spool file. So a pass that moves k fronts reads the whole spool 1+k times.
